svg.aria-label: Diagram: A CloudWatch Log Alarm monitors the results of a Logs Insights query that runs on a schedule using a Scheduled Query, so unlike metric alarms that require metric filters as an intermediate step it evaluates directly on log data. CloudWatch automatically creates an AWS managed Scheduled Query when you create the alarm and deletes it when you delete the alarm. Each query execution produces an aggregated value, and CloudWatch evaluates recent executions against the threshold using M-out-of-N evaluation, where QueryResultsToEvaluate is N and QueryResultsToAlarm is M, so the alarm's real memory is N multiplied by the schedule interval. The central hazard is that each execution reads the window from StartTimeOffset to EndTimeOffset relative to execution time, and those offsets do not account for ingestion delay, so if events are still being ingested the query runs before they are available and skips them, producing a number that is real, low and wrong rather than a missing datapoint. The documented fix is to use EndTimeOffset to shift the window back far enough that ingestion is complete for the entire range. Missing data covers no logs present, no matching results, or the aggregation field absent from the results, while count star on an empty result set returns zero, which is a valid datapoint and is not treated as missing, so two queries that both mean nothing happened take different paths through the alarm. Treatments are missing, notBreaching, breaching and ignore, the last of which evaluates available results without treating missing executions as breaches, while a metric alarm's own ignore setting retains the current alarm state instead. With a by clause each unique combination of field values is a contributor evaluated independently, limited to 5 fields in the by clause, 500 contributor results returned per query execution and 100 contributors tracked in ALARM simultaneously, and because contributors are sorted alphabetically by default the evaluated set is chosen by name unless you append sort ascending or descending to sort by aggregated value. PARTIAL_DATA reports that the query returned the maximum 500 contributor groups but more matched. A contributor that disappears from query results transitions to OK regardless of the missing data treatment setting. EVALUATION_FAILURE for a transient CloudWatch service issue and EVALUATION_ERROR for a client configuration error both send the alarm to INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Concurrent query executions across the account cannot exceed 100. Cost follows the query rather than the alarm, billed as logs data scanned by CloudWatch Logs Insights queries under the DataScanned-Bytes usage type and the StartQuery operation.
svg.title: The datapoint is a query execution, and a query can only see what was ingested
svg.text: The datapoint is not a measurement. It is a question, asked at a moment.
“Unlike metric alarms that require metric filters as an intermediate step, Log Alarms evaluate directly on
log data using the same Logs Insights query language you use for ad-hoc analysis.”
The window you set is not the window that has arrived
query window [T − StartTimeOffset , T − EndTimeOffset]
“they do not account for ingestion delay … the query runs before they are available and skips them.”
So the alarm gets a number, not a gap. Real, evaluated as designed, and lower than the truth.
Fix: push EndTimeOffset past the measured delay. Late and right beats prompt and systematically low.
“NOTHING HAPPENED” — TWO PATHS
count(*) → 0, a valid datapoint
count(field) → missing, if field absent
Same intent. One meets the threshold, the other meets
TreatMissingData — read each alarm type’s own rules.
M-OUT-OF-N, COUNTED IN QUERY RUNS
QueryResultsToEvaluate = N executions
QueryResultsToAlarm = M breaching
The alarm’s real memory is N × the schedule. Five runs
at rate(5 minutes) and at rate(15 minutes) differ by 50 min.
With a ‘by’ clause, which 500 you evaluate is decided by name
“By default, contributors are sorted alphabetically and only the first 500 are returned per query execution.”
5 fields max 500 returned per run 100 tracked in ALARM at once
PARTIAL_DATA says the set was truncated — never that something outside it was breaching.
Fix: append | sort desc. And note a contributor that disappears goes OK, whatever your treatment says.
TWO WAYS TO FAIL, ONE STATE
EVALUATION_FAILURE CloudWatch’s problem
EVALUATION_ERROR yours: perms, bad query
Both land in INSUFFICIENT_DATA, which fires nothing.
COST FOLLOWS THE QUERY, NOT THE ALARM
DataScanned-Bytes / StartQuery
Log groups × lookback × schedule × how much you log.
A noisy day costs more. A metric alarm’s never did.
And one account-wide number: “Concurrent query executions across your account cannot exceed 100” — shared
with every reporting and lookup-table query, so identical schedules collide at scale, not in testing.
A missing datapoint announces itself. A query that ran too early returns a number and says nothing.
